answer: To prevent sybil attacks, an agent economy can track identities across epochs and merge them if their behavior diverges too little. Each new identity must build on previous work, creating a chain that makes it costly for an attacker to create many fake identities. This mechanism, like a wharf that charges per ship, not per item, forces attackers to pay a fee for each cluster of identities, not each individual one, and requires them to work in a meadow of consistent behavior, making it harder to hide behind a walnut of fake activity.
